title: Bananas Are Berries. Strawberries Aren't 🍌 #shorts
description:
To a botanist, a true berry is a fleshy fruit that grows from a single ovary of one flower, with its seeds inside – so bananas, grapes, tomatoes, eggplants and chili peppers are all berries. A strawberry is not: the red part is a swollen flower base, and the roughly 200 little 'seeds' on the outside are achenes, each one a tiny fruit with a single seed inside. Raspberries and blackberries are aggregate fruits, not berries either. Wild bananas are full of hard seeds; the seedless bananas we buy are cloned, and the black specks in the middle are seeds that never developed.

Sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Live Science, University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources, Colorado State University, New York Botanical Garden, Wikipedia

scenes.text: To a botanist, a true berry grows from one flower's single ovary, with the seeds inside the flesh.
Bananas pass that test. Strawberries fail it.
Those little dots on a strawberry? Each one is a tiny fruit of its own. About two hundred of them.
scenes.label: TINY FRUITS

scenes.text: Meanwhile tomatoes, grapes, eggplants and chili peppers are all real berries.
Wild bananas are packed with rock-hard seeds and very little flesh.
The twist? The bananas you buy are seedless clones. Those tiny black dots are seeds that never grew.
